subject: Operator runbook and evacuation triggers for multi-region private deploy (EU ↔ APAC)

Subject: Operator runbook and evacuation triggers for private deploy (EU/APAC)

Hi Marcus / team,

Thanks again for the walkthrough last week. Our regulators are asking for a documented operator runbook that covers a planned cross-region evacuation from our EU private cluster into APAC standby (and the fallback path). They specifically want:

- Clear failover triggers (automated + manual) and the exact operator steps.
- Custody/ownership for KMS keys during the failover window.
- Evidence we can hand to auditors (logs, DocuSign approvals, timeline).
- Expected RTO/RPO and the customer-visible latency increase during the evacuation.

We'd like to run a dry-run before the end of October. Can you send a draft operator runbook (play-by-play) and an acceptance checklist? Also flag any constraints we should expect (IP whitelisting, BGP propagation delays, and any temporary data-copy retention policies).

Attachments: satori_compliance_qna_v3.pdf (our questionnaire)

Regards,
Lucy Chang
Head of Cloud Ops, Satori Bank
lucy@satori-bank.com

Subject: Re: Operator runbook and evacuation triggers for private deploy (EU/APAC)

Lucy — thanks for the clear ask. We can draft a three-phase runbook and an acceptance checklist for the dry-run:

Phase A (Prepare): inventory and prechecks (KMS key sync status, replication lag, route maps, BGP sessions established), obtain two named authorizations (Satori CloudOps + Satori Security), set a pre-run snapshot window.

Phase B (Evacuate): operator steps to route traffic to APAC (announce APAC prefixes, adjust NAT/Egress tagging, swap KMS key access policy to temporary wrap key), monitor KV cache warm-up, and ramp traffic in 10% increments with canary verification.

Phase C (Fallback / Reconcile): return traffic to EU, validate data parity, close the authorization window, and publish audit logs.

I'll attach our internal starter template (evacuation_runbook_v1.pdf) and a simple KMS mapping (kms_keymap_v2.xlsx). Vanessa and Irene — can you add operational notes on BGP and the audit checklist respectively?

Proposed dry-run windows: 2026-10-18 or 2026-10-25 (EU night / APAC morning). Which works for Satori?

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Director, Private Deployments | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: evacuation_runbook_v1.pdf, kms_keymap_v2.xlsx

Subject: Re: Operator runbook and evacuation triggers for private deploy (EU/APAC)

Adding ops-level details on routing and observable expectations. High-level items to include in the runbook:

- BGP and route advertisment: announce APAC prefixes from standby VPC; expected propagation: 30s–5min for most peers, but allow a 15 min window for peripheral ISPs.
- Egress SNAT / IP continuity: we'll add temporary egress SNAT to minimize source IP churn. Note: some upstreams will see a different ASN — we should flag any IP allowlists.
- Health-checks & canary gating: use the same cookie/canary endpoints we discussed; failover should pause if error rate > 2% for 3 consecutive minutes.
- KV cache warm-up: expect initial latency spike 40–250ms per token for first 30s as caches populate, then plateau.
- Metrics to collect: per-route p50/p95 latency, token-rate, KV hit-rate, BGP state changes, KMS error counts.

Constraints / tradeoffs:
- Cross-region egress cost during evacuation can be material if we keep data-synchronization window large. Recommend 1 hour retention window for fallback reconciliation unless compliance requires longer.
- Some legacy on-prem integration points may need manual firewall updates — list to be validated with Satori.

Lucy — if you can share Satori's allowlist and the upstream ASN info, I can run a latency/propagation sim for the proposed dates.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Network Reliability Engineer | Redwood Inference

Lucy / team — from a security & compliance perspective I'm outlining the acceptance checklist and the evidence package we'll produce for the regulator: 

Acceptance checklist (must be green to sign-off):
1) Pre-run: KMS replication status shows 0 un-synced keys; all customer key aliases resolved.
2) Authorization: signed runbook approvals from Satori CloudOps and Satori Security (DocuSign record linked).
3) Observability: continuous audit logging enabled and shipped to the audit S3 bucket for the run window.
4) Canary tests: pass at least 3 consecutive canary checks at full canary traffic.
5) Post-run: data parity verification report and md5 manifests for any copied artifacts.

Evidence package we will hand over (CSV/PDF):
- Operator action log (timestamps + operator id + action hashes)
- BGP announcement timeline and AS-path snapshots
- KMS access logs and temporary key-wrapping records
- Canary test results and traffic shift graphs
- DocuSign approvals (signed)

Notes on KMS custody: Redwood will not export raw customer keys. During the evacuation we use a temporary key-wrapping policy where Satori retains master key custody in their KMS; Redwood will request wrapped-key access with a short TTL (recommended 2 hours) and all unwraps are logged. We can include the unwrap audit extracts in the evidence package.

Link to runbook draft and evidence checklist: https://drive.redwood.com/teams/ops/evacuation_runbook_v1
DocuSign envelope: DocuSign:DS-983722-Agreement

Proposed next step: Marcus / Vanessa to sync with Satori on the allowlist and the ASN details, I will prepare the evidence template for the dry-run.

— Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.com
